chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from 'Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Yunus, from Yazid ibn Khalifah, who said:
I said to Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام: Indeed, 'Umar ibn Hanzalah came to us from you with a time. He said: So Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام said: Then he does not lie against us.

I said: He said, the time of maghrib is when the disk disappears, except that the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, when travel pressed hard upon him, would delay maghrib and combine it with the later 'isha'.
So he said: He spoke the truth. And he said: The time of 'isha' is when the twilight disappears until one-third of the night, and the time of fajr is when it appears until it becomes bright.

key_terms.الشَّفَقُ: the twilight whose disappearance marks the beginning of 'isha' time
key_terms.الْفَجْرِ: the fajr salat (prayer), beginning with the appearance of dawn
key_terms.الْقُرْصُ: the sun's disk whose disappearance marks maghrib time
key_terms.الْمَغْرِبِ: the maghrib salat (prayer), beginning at sunset
key_terms.ثُلُثِ اللَّيْلِ: one-third of the night, marking the end of the stated 'isha' time
key_terms.وَقْتُ: the appointed time or legal time for an act of worship

ai.seo_question: What are the times of maghrib, 'isha', and fajr according to this hadith in al-Istibsar?
ai.summary: This hadith states the times for maghrib, 'isha', and fajr, and confirms the report transmitted by 'Umar ibn Hanzalah. It also notes that the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم would at times delay maghrib and combine it with 'isha' when urgently traveling, indicating permissibility in such a circumstance.
